newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore HSFO rangebound, N.Asian supplies ample.
newsitem.headline: Singapore HSFO rangebound, N.Asian supplies ample.

text.p: High sulphur fuel oil prices on Friday were expected to be rangebound, hovering around Thursday's range of $121-$123 per tonne for 180-cst supplies loading in November, traders said.
Chinese buyers have returned to enquire about November cargoes after they temporarily slowed imports when prices started to rise in early October, traders said.
Traders said fuel oil stocks in China are low and Chinese buyers have to increase imports.
Bids into southern China were heard at $127 per tonne or at a $5-$6 per tonne premium over Singapore spot quotes on a cost-and-freight basis.
A 20,000 tonne distressed cargo of 180-cst for loading from South Korean in October was sold earlier this week but price details were not immediately available.
Traders said two more distressed October cargoes were still seeking homes, one from a South Korean refiner and another from a Japanese trader.
In the swaps market, October fuel oil was discussed at $121/$122, barely changed from Wednesday's $120.50/$121
